summary: An interface lists methods a class promises to write. An abstract class can share real code but still leave some methods for subclasses, and you cannot create objects from it.
notes: A class extends one class but can implement many interfaces: class Quiz extends Assignment implements Gradable, Comparable<Quiz>.
Interface methods are public, so percent() in Quiz and Project must be declared public.
%% in String.format prints a single percent sign.
pitfall: Leaving percent() out of Quiz fails to compile with "Quiz is not abstract and does not override abstract method percent() in Gradable".
